"Saudi Arabia says 1 dead, 11 injured in latest attack on Riyadh airport"
BYLINE: "By Al Jazeera Staff, AP and Reuters" - AP and Reuters attribution. Photo credit: Saudi Ministry of Media via Reuters.

A projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, killing one and injuring 11, per the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA). GACA identified the dead as a PAKISTANI RESIDENT; injured transferred to several hospitals.
The strike hit TERMINALS 3 AND 4, which serve domestic flights.
India's embassy said one of its citizens died on Sunday of injuries from Saturday's attack, BRINGING THE DEATH TOLL TO 13.
A witness on board a taxiing aircraft told Reuters a projectile struck the tarmac next to several parked planes at about 8:30pm (17:30 GMT) Sunday, causing a fire. The aircraft returned to the gate and passengers were told to leave.

KEY FIGURE: "The Riyadh airport has been struck FOUR TIMES IN THE PAST FIVE DAYS." Houthi attacks on King Khalid airport on THURSDAY killed at least three Saudi citizens including a pilot (GACA).
The airport has been CLOSED since Saturday's attack - the deadliest in the country since the US-Israel war on Iran began in late February.
IMPORTANT CAVEAT: "The Houthis claimed responsibility for the strikes BEFORE Sunday's." (i.e. Sunday's strike not claimed at time of writing - conflicts with the BBC framing.)

Trump says he is weighing whether to join the fight against the Houthis. He had said he intends to speak with Saudi Crown Prince MOHAMMED BIN SALMAN, who is seeking help against the Houthis, "but there were no signs on Sunday that the US president had followed up on his claim."
The escalation puts further pressure on global oil supplies and prices, and on commercial shipping through the BAB AL-MANDEB strait off Yemen - a crucial alternative waterway to the Strait of Hormuz. Fears US intervention could prompt the Houthis to halt shipping through Bab al-Mandeb. The rebels seized key areas along the strait last month; the Saudi-led coalition has been trying to retake them.
